text:
maya: quick ask — staging canary is showing a 12% tail-latency increase on 2.1.0 compared to 2.0.7. can we do a fast sanity and either approve proceed or hold+rollback?

chris: looking now. can you paste the p95/p99 numbers and which route?

maya: p95 ~ 220ms -> 240ms, p99 ~ 480ms -> 540ms on /v1/generate (default model pool). spike starts at ~10:12 UTC when rollout hit 10% traffic.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: canary v2.1.0 -> 10% traffic at 2027-01-12T10:09:41Z. Health checks passed.

samir: I pulled a flamegraph from the staging replica that reported the highest latency. top hot path is KV cache miss handling + attention kernel stall. attaching snippet: `
# top stacks (sample)
1 36%  kv_cache_lookup
2 22%  attention_kernel
3 8%   tokenizer
`

ellie: do we have any config drift? batching params, max_batch_size or batch_timeout changed in this rollout?

chris: config is identical. the main change was switching to fused-attn kernel 3.2 which matches perf bench notes. locally perf bench on same gpu didn't show p99 regressions though.

maya: interesting — could be workload distribution in staging causing fewer prefix cache hits. samir any quick check for cache hit rate?

samir: cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 62% on that host after rollout. looks like tokenization differences caused different prefixes hashed.

harry: recommendation: pause the remainder of rollout immediately and spin a job to rewarm the cache on impacted hosts. agree to hold until we see hit rate >70% and p99 within 10% of baseline. :thumbsup:

maya: pausing rollout now (manual hold). @deploy-bot can you mark rollout paused?

deploy-bot: Rollout status: PAUSED by maya at 2027-01-12T10:23:15Z. Current traffic stays at 10%.

chris: I'll run a small rewarm script across the 3 affected nodes and rerun the p99 smoke. command: `for host in a b c; do ./replay_prefixes --hosts $host --file top_prefixes.log; done`

samir: also submitting a perf trace ticket with profiler dump -> TKT-4247. I included the flamegraph and cache stats.

ellie: if rewarm doesn't help we should rollback to 2.0.7. please add clear rollback checklist in the ticket so oncall can execute quickly.

maya: agreed. plan: (1) rewarm + smoke, (2) if p99 <= +10% and hitrate >=70% then resume; (3) else rollback and notify infra + cs. I've created the doc: https://redwood.internal/notes/canary-1793456789 (private).

harry: I can approve the resume if checks pass. ping me once results are in.

chris: first smoke done — p95 235ms, p99 510ms (baseline p99 480). hit rate now 71% on those nodes. rewarming helped a lot.

maya: thanks. harry — can you give a green for resume?

harry: green from infra side. resume but keep automated rollback window at 60m and 10% steps.

deploy-bot: Rollout action: RESUME by maya at 2027-01-12T10:58:50Z. Next step will increase to 25% traffic in 10 minutes per policy.

maya: closing loop — will monitor p99 for 30m and email SRE if drift continues. great teamwork. :raised_hands:
